newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan stocks end down despite Wall Street gains.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan stocks end down despite Wall Street gains.

text.p: Taiwan share prices closed lower on Tuesday despite an early upsurge spurred by Wall Street's gains overnight, but brokers said prices should trend higher.
The index ended down 40.02 points or 0.61 percent at 6,478.44, off from an earlier high of 6,552.27.
Turnover was an active T$47.61 billion.
Brokers said an early rise reversed after the index neared technical resistance at 6,560 points.
"After the index's recent gains, investors turned cautious as fundamentals have shown little improvement," said Michael Hung of Nikko Securities.
"Only several industries such as personal computers, polyester fibre and construction have shown improvement. We haven't seen an overall recovery," Hung said.
Financials, which led recent gains, fell most, with Chinatrust down 50 cents to T$52.5 and Cathay Life down T$3 to T$175. Plastics, constructions and textiles also fell.
Electronics rose on Wall Street gains boosted by rising U.S. high-tech shares, with Holtek Microelectronics up T$1 to 31.9.
"The global PC market had 18 percent and 16 percent sales growth in the first and second quarter of 1996, respectively, and its 1997 outlook is optimistic," Hung said.
Shares in some domestic demand-oriented industries like steel, glass and automobiles, reflecting government efforts to boost the domestic economy, brokers said.
Brokers attributed the recent index gains to rising inflows of foreign equity funds and the dramatic gains on Wall Street.
"If Wall Street continues to rise, it will be a locomotive pushing our domestic index to test 6,600," Hung said, citing the next significant psychological resistance level.
Hung said speculation that the U.S. Federal Reserve might tighten monetary policy would not dampen the stock market much.
"Even if the Fed hikes rates, it will be at most 0.25 to 0.50 percentage points due to not-so-serious inflation. This should not have much impact on our stock market," Hung said.
Several brokers said they still expected an uptrend.
"In the near term, the index is likely to see range trading between 6,350 and 6,550, but in the mid and long-term, a gradual firming trend is expected," he said.
